title: The Jewish Physician’s Tale: The Young Man from Mosul and the Murdered Girl

paragraphs.en: In Damascus during my medical studies, a Mamluk from the governor's household summoned me to his home. There, I found a handsome young man lying ill in bed. Despite his high status, his manners seemed lacking as he only offered a subtle nod instead of a handshake.
paragraphs.zh: 在大马士革求学期间，一位来自总督府的马穆鲁克把我叫到他家里。在那里，我见到一个英俊的年轻人病倒在床。尽管他的身份显赫，举止却显得有些欠缺礼貌，只是微微点了点头，没有伸出手来握手。

paragraphs.en: After examining him and writing a prescription, I visited daily for ten days until he recovered sufficiently to bathe.
paragraphs.zh: 诊查完毕并开了药方之后，我连续十天每天探望，直到他恢复到可以洗澡的程度。

paragraphs.en: In the private bath, I noticed that his right hand was missing, causing me great concern. His body bore marks of recent beatings, now barely visible. As my worry grew, the young man sensed it and promised to share his story later.
paragraphs.zh: 在私人浴室里，我注意到他右手缺失，这让我非常担忧。他的身上留有最近遭受毒打的痕迹，现在已经几乎看不出来了。随着我的焦虑日益增加，年轻人似乎察觉到了，承诺稍后会讲述他的故事。

paragraphs.en: We then walked through the Damascus Gardens, enjoying the scenery before settling down for a meal.
paragraphs.zh: 我们随后漫步在大马士革花园中，欣赏着美景，随后找了个地方坐下用餐。

paragraphs.en: Just as I was about to ask him about his condition, he preempted me by saying, "Doctor, let me tell you my tale at the right moment."
paragraphs.zh: 正当我打算问他身体怎么样时，他抢先说道：“医生，请允许我在适当的时候讲述我的故事。”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad continued her tale on the one hundred and thirty-second night. She said, "I heard that the Jewish physician told the king of China about a young man from Mosul who had grown up among his uncles. One Friday, after prayers at the mosque, he and his father and uncles discussed foreign lands, particularly Cairo.
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹继续讲述她的故事，到了第一百三十二个夜晚。她说：“我听说那位犹太医生向中国国王提起过一个来自摩苏尔的年轻人，他自小在叔叔们的身边长大。在一个周五，祷告完毕后，他和他的父亲以及叔叔们讨论起外国的风土人情，特别是开罗。”

paragraphs.en: They argued over which city was most beautiful—Cairo or Baghdad—but his father insisted that Cairo was essential to see."
paragraphs.zh: 他们争论哪个城市更美丽——开罗还是巴格达，但他的父亲坚持认为开罗是一定要去看的。

paragraphs.en: The physician's father said, "He who has not seen Cairo has not seen the world. Its dust is gold, its women dolls, and its Nile a wonder." He quoted a poet:
paragraphs.zh: 医生的父亲说：“未到开罗者，未见真世界。其尘若金，其女如 doll，尼罗河奇绝。”他引述了一位诗人的诗句：

paragraphs.en: "Enjoy today the flooding of your Nile, Whose waters on you their riches bestow. The Nile is but the tears I shed for you, A boon, which from my blighted eyes does flow."
paragraphs.zh: “尽情享受今日尼罗河的泛滥，它的waters将财富赐予你。尼罗河不过是为汝而洒下的泪水，这是从我这枯萎的眼中流出的恩赐。”

paragraphs.en: He described Cairo's beauty, mentioning its gardens adorned with flowers and the Nile Island. He compared it to a sabre in an eye trembling with fright, emphasizing how stunning the green gardens encircled by the waters of the Nile looked.
paragraphs.zh: 他描绘了开罗的美丽，提到了那里繁花似锦的花园和尼罗河岛。他将这一切比作一把利剑插入眼中，那双惊恐的眼睛显得格外动人，强调那些被尼罗河水环绕的翠绿花园是多么令人惊叹。

paragraphs.en: The young man was captivated by these descriptions and longed to see Cairo for himself.
paragraphs.zh: 这个年轻人被这些描述深深吸引，渴望亲自看看开罗。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: "I heard, O King, that the Jewish physician told the king of China about the young man from Mosul. He described Cairo, mentioning the Nile and the Ethiopian Pond. But what struck him most were the observatory's wonders and the beauty of al-Rauda Park in late afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 我听国王说，那位犹太医生向中国国王讲述了来自摩苏尔的年轻人的故事。他提到了开罗，提及了尼罗河和埃塞俄比亚池塘。但让他印象最深的还是天文台的奇观以及傍晚时分阿尔劳达公园的美景。

paragraphs.en: The sunset on the riverbank, with the Nile shimmering like armor, left a lasting impression."
paragraphs.zh: 河岸边的夕阳映照在尼罗河上，波光粼粼犹如铠甲般闪耀，留下了深刻的印象。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹阿德接着说：

paragraphs.en: "When I heard this vivid description, my thoughts lingered on Cairo all night long."
paragraphs.zh: 当听到这番生动的描述时，我的思绪整晚都萦绕在开罗。

paragraphs.en: Some time later, my uncles prepared goods for a trade journey to Cairo. I begged my father until he agreed to send me along with them. He warned my uncles not to take me to Cairo but to sell my merchandise in Damascus instead.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一段时间，我的叔叔们准备了一些货物，打算前往开罗进行贸易。我央求父亲，直到他答应让我和他们一起去。不过，父亲警告叔叔们不要带我去开罗，在大马士革卖掉我的货物比较安全。

paragraphs.en: We left Mosul and traveled through Aleppo before reaching Damascus. The city was beautiful, filled with trees, rivers, and birds, like a garden in Paradise. I rented a large house from Sudun ‘Abd al-Rahman for two dinars a month.
paragraphs.zh: 我们离开了摩苏尔，途经阿勒颇，最终抵达了大马士革。这座城市美丽非凡，绿树成荫，河流潺潺，鸟语花香，仿佛人间仙境一般。我每月支付两第纳尔从苏杜恩·阿卜杜勒-拉赫曼那里租下了一所大房子。

paragraphs.en: It had a marble hall, storeroom, extra room with cupboards, and a fountain running day and night.
paragraphs.zh: 它有一个大理石大堂、储藏室，还有一间带橱柜的额外房间，并且日夜不停地流淌着泉水。

paragraphs.en: I spent my days feasting and drinking until most of my money was gone. One day, as I sat at the door of my house, a young woman in fine clothing arrived. She agreed to come inside, much to my surprise.
paragraphs.zh: 我整天沉迷于宴饮之中，直到花光了大部分的钱财。有一天，当我坐在家门口时，一位穿着华丽的年轻女子出现了。令我惊讶的是，她竟然同意走进我的屋子里。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued her story: "O happy King, I heard that the Jewish physician told the king of China about the young man's encounter with a beautifully dressed lady."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹继续讲述：“哦，幸福的国王，我听说那位犹太医生向中国国王讲述了那个年轻人与一位打扮得十分漂亮的女士相遇的故事。”

paragraphs.en: Upon her arrival, I felt compelled to honor the invitation and entered, closing the door behind us. She removed her veil and cloak, revealing an extraordinary beauty that captivated my heart. I bought delicacies and wine from a special shop and set up for our feast.
paragraphs.zh: 她一进门，我就感到有必要接受邀请，跟着她进了屋，并随手关上了门。她摘下了面纱和斗篷，露出的是一副令人心动的绝美容颜。我特意去了一家专门店买了些精致的小吃和美酒，为我们的盛宴做了准备。

paragraphs.en: We ate, drank, and conversed until we were drunk. That night, she left with ten dinars, insisting on returning in three days to prepare a similar banquet.
paragraphs.zh: 我们边吃边喝边聊天，直到酩酊大醉。那天晚上，她带着十迪纳尔离开了，并坚持要在三天后回来举办类似的盛宴。

paragraphs.en: Three days later, I prepared another lavish meal. She arrived after sundown, wearing wooden shoes and a black headcloth, her presence fragrant. We feasted and laughed until dark, when we drank until drunk again.
paragraphs.zh: 三天后，我又准备了一顿丰盛的晚餐。她傍晚时分 arrive 后才出现，穿着木鞋和黑色头巾，身上散发着淡淡的香气。我们边吃边笑，直到夜幕降临，然后又喝得酩酊大醉。

paragraphs.en: That night, she returned with ten more dinars, promising to bring a younger, even more beautiful lady.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，她又带着十枚第纳尔回来了，并承诺会带来一位更加年轻、更加美丽的女士。

paragraphs.en: Three days passed, and I prepared another banquet. When she arrived as usual, she proposed bringing a young woman who had been secluded for a long time. I agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 三天过去了，我又准备了一场宴会。她像往常一样到来时，提议带一位长期被隔离的年轻女子一同前来。我欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, she left with fifteen dinars, instructing me to buy more provisions for their upcoming meeting.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天早上，她带着十五个第纳尔离开了，并吩咐我为他们即将举行的会面购买更多的补给品。

paragraphs.en: The next evening, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹朵开始说道：

paragraphs.en: "I heard that the Jewish physician told the king about a young man from Mosul who met a murdered girl. The next night, she arrived as planned with the girl. I welcomed them warmly, lit the candles, and when the girl unveiled herself, her beauty was breathtaking.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说那位犹太医生向国王讲述了一个来自摩苏尔的年轻人与一名遇害女孩的故事。到了晚上，女孩如约而至。我热情地迎接了他们，点燃蜡烛，当那女孩揭开面纱时，她的美丽令人惊叹。

paragraphs.en: We ate together, and I fed her while she smiled at me. After dinner, we drank wine and fruits, and she winked at me, captivating my heart. My friend noticed our mutual attraction and playfully asked if I preferred this visitor over her.
paragraphs.zh: 我们一同用餐，她边笑边由我喂食。晚餐后，我们品尝了酒和水果，她调皮地向我眨眼，深深吸引了我的心。我的朋友注意到了我们之间的默契，开玩笑地说我不是在更喜欢这位客人胜过她吗？

paragraphs.en: I admitted that the girl was indeed more beautiful. She then suggested sleeping with her, to which I agreed. Later, she prepared a bed for herself in another room while I slept with the new arrival."
paragraphs.zh: 我承认那女孩确实更加美丽。接着她建议和我同眠，对此我欣然同意。之后，她在另一个房间为自己准备了床铺，而我自己则与新来的客人共寝。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹阿德接着说：

paragraphs.en: "By morning, Dinarzad had learned of my encounter and our shared feelings."
paragraphs.zh: 到早上，迪纳兹已经知道了我和他之间的相遇以及我们共同的感受。

paragraphs.en: When I awoke in the morning, I found myself drenched and thought it was from perspiration. Sitting up, I tried to rouse the girl but when I shook her by the shoulders, her head rolled off, revealing she had been murdered. Panicked, I cried out "O gracious Protector" and sprang up, only for the world to turn black before my eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 当我清晨醒来时，发现自己全身湿透，以为是汗水。坐起身来，我试着唤醒那女孩，但当我在她肩膀上摇晃时，她的头颅滚落下来，露出了她已被谋杀的事实。我惊恐万分，脱口喊道：“仁慈的保护者！”然后猛地站起，眼前却突然一片漆黑。

paragraphs.en: Realizing it was my friend who had committed the murder out of jealousy, I thought, "There is no power but in God." I feared the girl's family would seek revenge and decided to act quickly.
paragraphs.zh: 意识到是朋友出于嫉妒犯下了谋杀罪，我心想：“除了上帝，别无力量可言。”我担心女孩的家人会寻求报复，决定迅速行动。

paragraphs.en: I undressed, dug a hole in the hall, placed the girl with her jewelry inside, covered it with earth, and replaced the marble slabs. After putting on clean clothes, I took what was left of my money and locked up the house before leaving. At the landlord's, I paid a year’s rent and claimed to be joining my uncles in Cairo.
paragraphs.zh: 我脱掉了衣服，在大厅挖了个坑，把那女孩连同她的首饰一起放了进去，然后用泥土覆盖，重新铺上了大理石地板。换上干净的衣服后，我收拾好剩余的钱财，锁上门离开了。在房东那里，我付了一年的房租，并谎称要去开罗与我的叔叔们团聚。

paragraphs.en: Then, at the king’s caravansary, I paid for my voyage and departed.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，在国王的驿站里，我付清了旅费，便启程上路了。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; this is nothing compared to what I will tell you if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹阿德默然不语。丁纳札德说道：“姐姐，这真是个奇异而引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹阿德回答道：“等到明天晚上再说吧；如果国王饶恕了我，我会给你讲一个更精彩的故事。”

paragraphs.en: I arrived in Cairo safely and stayed with my uncles for three years, enjoying the city but squandering all my money on feasts and drinks. When they left, I hid until they departed, then returned to Cairo for another year, sending rent to Damascus.
paragraphs.zh: 我平安抵达开罗，与叔叔们住了三年，虽然享受着这座城市的繁华，却把所有的钱都花在了宴会上和酒水中。等他们离开后，我躲藏了一段时间，随后又回到了开罗，又过了一年的时间，并定期向大马士革寄去房租。

paragraphs.en: After returning to Damascus, I found the landlord, a jeweler, who welcomed me warmly. I entered the house, swept it clean, and discovered a gold necklace with ten gemstones under the bed where I had slept with the murdered girl. Recognizing it, I wept for a long time before cleaning the house and restoring its furniture.
paragraphs.zh: 回到大马士革后，我找到了那位珠宝商房东，他热情地接待了我。我进了屋，把房间打扫干净，在我和被害女孩曾共眠的床下发现了一条金项链，上面镶着十颗宝石。看到这条项链，我不禁泪流满面，足足哭了好一会儿。之后，我才开始清理房屋并恢复家具原状。

paragraphs.en: For two days, I stayed at home, then went to the bath, rested, and changed into fresh clothes. With no money left, fate and temptation led me to take the necklace, wrap it in a handkerchief, and sell it to a broker who praised its quality and value, promising a prosperous start to my business.
paragraphs.zh: 连续两天，我待在家里，然后去了澡堂洗了个澡，休息了一番，换上了干净的衣服。囊中羞涩之下，命运和诱惑让我起了贪念，拿走了那串项链，用手帕包好，卖给了一位商人。那位商人称赞项链质地优良，价值不菲，并许诺这将是我的事业的良好开端。

paragraphs.en: The broker took me to the landlord's shop, where I sat by his side, setting the stage for what was to come.
paragraphs.zh: 经纪人带我来到房东的店铺，我坐在他身旁，为接下来的故事做起了铺垫。

paragraphs.en: We waited until the market was bustling. The broker took the necklace secretly and sold it for two thousand dinars without my knowledge. He returned, saying the necklace was fake and he received only a thousand dirhams.
paragraphs.zh: 我们等到市场熙熙攘攘时，那经纪人悄悄地拿走了项链，并在我不知情的情况下以两千第纳尔卖掉了它。他回来时说这条项链是假的，只收到了一千迪拉姆。

paragraphs.en: I accepted his offer, knowing it was brass.
paragraphs.zh: 我接受了他的话，心里明白那不过是一句空话。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, calamity struck. Officers seized me while I sat in my shop. They accused me of stealing the necklace and beat me until I confessed under torture.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，灾祸降临。当我坐在店铺里时，警察将我逮捕。他们指控我偷走了那串项链，并对我施以毒打，直到我在酷刑下供出了实情。

paragraphs.en: My hand was cut off, and when they seared it with boiling oil, I fainted for half a day. When I regained consciousness, my landlord told me to leave his house.
paragraphs.zh: 我的一只手被砍掉了，当他们用沸油烫伤它时，我昏迷了一整天。等我苏醒过来，房东告诉我必须离开他的房子。

paragraphs.en: Disappointed, I asked for three days to find another place. He agreed but left, sad and worried about how he would explain my situation to our people. I wept bitterly.
paragraphs.zh: 失望之下，我请求再给我三天时间另寻住处。他答应了，但显得忧心忡忡，担心如何向我们的族人解释我的处境。我痛哭流涕。

paragraphs.en: That night, Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if you want more."
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，沙赫拉兹阿德默然不语。丁尔札德说道：“姐姐，这真是个奇怪而有趣的故事！”沙赫拉兹阿德回答说：“如果你还想听更多，那就等到明天晚上吧。”

paragraphs.en: I fell ill for two days before the landlord and a chief merchant arrived at my door, accompanied by five police officers. They accused me of stealing a necklace that had belonged to the governor of Damascus, who claimed it was missing along with his daughter for three years. My heart sank as they bound me and placed a collar around my neck attached to a chain.
paragraphs.zh: 我连续两天生病，房东和一位大商人在五名警察的陪同下敲开了我的门。他们指控我偷走了 Damascus 总督的一串项链，总督声称三年前他的女儿和那串项链一同失踪了。听到这些指控，我的心沉了下来，随后被绑了起来，并戴上了颈圈，上面挂着一条铁链。

paragraphs.en: I covered my face, vowing to tell the governor my true story. If he wished, I would accept his judgment—whether death or mercy.
paragraphs.zh: 我捂住脸，发誓要向总督讲述我的真实经历。如果他愿意，我可以接受他的裁决——无论是死刑还是宽恕。

paragraphs.en: They brought me before the governor. He asked if I had taken his necklace to sell at the market. When I denied it and explained how I was falsely accused by a merchant who beat me, the governor declared, "Don't be afraid."
paragraphs.zh: 他们把我带到了总督面前。他问我是否把他的项链拿到市场上去卖了。我否认并解释说我被一个商贩冤枉还打了我才这么说的，总督闻言说道：“别害怕。”

paragraphs.en: He then sentenced the merchant to pay for my hand or face severe punishment.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后判决商人大卫赔偿我的聘礼钱，否则将面临严厉的惩罚。

paragraphs.en: Hearing this, I recounted the story of the young man from Mosul and the murdered girl. The girl had brought her own necklace, which she claimed belonged to her. Out of jealousy, she killed the girl at night.
paragraphs.zh: 听到这里，我讲述了来自摩苏尔的年轻人和那位遇害女孩的故事。那个女孩带来了她自己的项链，并声称那是她的。出于嫉妒，她在夜间将女孩杀害了。

paragraphs.en: The governor listened in silence, then shook his head and said, "To God we belong and to Him we return."
paragraphs.zh: 总督沉默片刻，然后摇了摇头，说道：“我们归于上帝，也必将归于上帝。”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused as morning approached. Dinarzad remarked on the story's strangeness, prompting Shahrazad to promise a more enthralling tale if she was spared for another night.
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹在晨光渐近时停下了讲述。丁纳扎德对这个故事感到有些奇怪，于是莎赫拉兹承诺，如果她能再留一夜的话，一定会讲一个更加引人入胜的故事。

paragraphs.en: The next evening, Shahrazad began her narrative again, eager to captivate the king once more.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹再次开始了她的讲述，渴望再度赢得国王的青睐。

paragraphs.en: The governor recounted his eldest daughter's tragic story. She had been brought up in strict seclusion before marrying her cousin in Cairo. After his son-in-law died, she returned with bad habits and visited the physician three or four times.
paragraphs.zh: 总督讲述了他长女的悲惨故事。她曾严格遵守闺阁之规，直到在开罗嫁给堂兄。丈夫去世后，她带回了一些不良习惯，并多次拜访那位医生。

paragraphs.en: Eventually, she brought her younger sister to him. The sisters were inseparable, but when the elder began an affair, she confided in her sister, who wished to visit as well. With permission granted, the younger sister came to see the physician.
paragraphs.zh: 最终，她把妹妹也带给了医生。两姐妹形影不离，但当姐姐开始一段恋情时，便向妹妹倾诉了自己的心事，并希望能一同前往求医。在得到许可后，妹妹也来到了医生的诊所。

paragraphs.en: Envious of her success with the young man, she murdered her sister and returned home without informing anyone.
paragraphs.zh: 嫉妒妹妹在那年轻人身上取得的成功，她暗中害死了自己的妹妹，然后悄然回家，没有告知任何人。

paragraphs.en: On the day they were supposed to eat together, the governor searched for his missing daughter but found only her weeping sister. The younger sister had left suddenly during prayer time, dressed in all her finery. Her elder sister waited anxiously, refusing food or drink, vowing never to stop crying until she died.
paragraphs.zh: 在他们本应共进晚餐的日子里，总督四处寻找失踪的女儿，却只找到了她哭泣的妹妹。妹妹是在祈祷时突然离家出走的，穿着一身盛装。姐姐焦急地等待着，连饭也不吃，发誓要一直哭下去直到死去。

paragraphs.en: This grief eventually drove her to suicide.
paragraphs.zh: 最终，这悲痛将她推向了自杀的深渊。

paragraphs.en: The governor concluded that such events underscore the fleeting nature of life and man's transient existence.
paragraphs.zh: governor总结道，这类事件凸显了生命的短暂和人类存在之瞬息万变。

paragraphs.en: The Jewish physician recounted his tale. His son had lost his right hand unjustly but was then offered marriage to the youngest daughter of a wealthy man. The father provided him with a dowry, clothes, and money, treating him like a son.
paragraphs.zh: 犹太医生讲述了他的故事。他的儿子原本无缘无故地失去了右手，但随后却得到了一位富人家最小女儿的婚事。父亲为他准备了嫁妆、衣物和钱财，待他如同亲生子一般。

paragraphs.en: After learning of his father's death, he received an edict from Egypt and returned home in prosperity.
paragraphs.zh: 得知父亲去世的消息后，他收到了埃及的诏令，荣归故里。

paragraphs.en: His story amazed me, and I stayed with him until he went to bathe again and returned to his wife. He gave me a sum of money and bid me farewell before sending me on my way. I journeyed eastward, eventually reaching Baghdad where I lived contentedly until the nightmarish encounter with the hunchback.
paragraphs.zh: 他的故事让我惊叹不已，我陪着他直到他再次去沐浴回来，并回到妻子身边。他给了我一笔钱，与我告别后便送我上路。我向东行进，最终抵达巴格达，在那里我过着平静的生活，直到遇到了那个驼背人的噩梦般遭遇。

paragraphs.en: Isn't this story more fascinating than that of the hunchback?
paragraphs.zh: 这故事比驼背人的故事有趣多了。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "What a strange and engaging tale!" Shahrazad replied, "This is nothing compared to what I will tell you tomorrow night if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹沉默下来。丁纳扎德remarked道：“这真是个奇怪而引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹回答说：“比起我明天晚上要讲给国王听的故事，这简直不算什么。如果国王饶恕我的话。”

paragraphs.en: The king, after hearing the Jewish physician's tale, shook his head and declared, "No, by God, it is not stranger than the hunchback’s story. I must kill all four of you for plotting to murder him. But you, tailor, as the chief offender, must tell a more wonderful, amazing, diverting, and entertaining story, or else your lives are forfeit."
paragraphs.zh: 国王听完犹太医生的故事后，摇了摇头，说道：“不，以真主的名义，这比驼背的故事还要离奇。我必须把你们四人全部处死，因为你们密谋要杀害他。不过你，裁缝，作为首要犯，必须讲一个更加奇妙、令人惊叹、引人入胜且有趣的 story，否则你们的命就没了。”

paragraphs.en: The tailor responded, "Very well."
paragraphs.zh: 裁缝回答说：“就这样吧。”

paragraphs.en: The king's decree hung heavily in the air, leaving no room for hesitation.
paragraphs.zh: 国王的命令如同阴云笼罩在空气中，留给人丝毫犹豫的空间也没有。
